result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: Section 337(a) covers an action on any contract, obligation or liability founded on a written instrument.
claims.quote: (a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing
claims.note: The stated scope is a claim on the written contract itself.

claims.claim: The time limit for that action is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The separate post-sale limit concerns secured obligations outside the stated scope.

claims.claim: Section 337(a) expressly excepts cases provided for in Section 336a.
claims.note: The draft does not claim what Section 336a provides.

claims.claim: Section 337 does not specify when the four-year period starts for the ordinary written-contract claim described.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: The applicable clause gives a duration but no starting event. The start dates in (b) and (c) concern account-stated and rescission claims, not the claim described.

result.summary: The supplied text supports both the four-year limit and the narrower statement that Section 337 gives no start date for the written-contract claim in scope.
